wy_southwest_shoulder.blurb: A single-pitch face of roughly 300 feet on the southwest side of Devils Tower, reached by the paved loop trail from the main lot. Crack systems take hand and finger jams, and most of the 15 climbs are traditional, with four short bolted lines and a pair of boulder problems. Grades start at easy 5.6 cracks and run up through the 5.9 and 5.11 range, so there is something for a newer leader and for someone after harder work. Plan on a standard trad rack, and watch for the odd loose flake. Descent is a simple walk-off back to the trail, which keeps days here short and relaxed.

wy_ufo_and_environs.blurb: A small cluster of boulders in the Rock Shop zone near Lander, built around one large, space-themed block that gives the area its name. All 15 problems are bouldering, with a broad spread: a handful of easy V0 to V2 lines for warming up, a solid middle of V4 to V6, and a few serious testpieces reaching into the V8 to V10 range. Elevation is above 8,000 feet, so it suits spring and fall best. Expect a short uphill trail from where the vehicle is left, and boulders described relative to the main block. Bring pads and a few friends to spot.

wy_upper_devil_s_playground.blurb: A small, rugged dome in the Vedauwoo area outside Laramie, a little east of Reynolds Hill and reached from the 700N side road. Bouldering is the main draw, with five problems from V3 up to V8, plus eight trad lines and a lone sport route mostly in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The stone is gritty and high-friction, rewarding finger strength and careful footwork. Boulders here are tall and landings steep, so bring several pads and spotters. It is windswept and quiet compared with the busier Vedauwoo crack crags, and late spring through early fall is the usual window.

wy_700s_boulders.blurb: A quiet, secluded bouldering spot in Vedauwoo, off the 700S side road near Laramie. Most of the 14 climbs are boulder problems, mainly cracks, with a couple of short trad lines. Grades run from V0 up to V8, with plenty of moderate problems in the V1 to V3 range and a few hard ones above V8. The approach is a short walk north from a small pullout, following a creek through an aspen grove. Crowds are rarely an issue, and there is room for more new lines. Bring pads and tape for the crack problems.

wy_north_face_northwest_corner.blurb: The shaded side of Devils Tower, and a good pick when the summer heat makes the sunny faces unpleasant. Most of the 14 routes are traditional crack climbs, plus two aid lines, with grades from 5.8 into the 5.12 range and a cluster around 5.11. Typical routes run about two pitches with rappel bolts, though a few continue to the summit, making them some of the longest on the Tower. Climbing on this side is steeper and harder than on the south. To reach it, follow the paved trail left past the west face, then branch off into the forest at a bench. Watch for poison ivy.

wy_central_gorge.blurb: A catch-all ice area in Shell Canyon, in the Bighorn Mountains, covering the stretch of gorge between Post Creek downstream and the Shell Falls and Brindle Falls zones upstream. Fourteen climbs, from WI2 to WI5, with a mix of moderate and hard flows and a few mixed or top-rope options. Getting in is the hard part: most flows sit across the fast, deep creek from the highway, so parties look for breaks in the cliffs or rappel in and leave a rope to climb back out. It is a place for self-reliant climbers who like route-finding and some commitment.

wy_cathedral_buttress.blurb: A big south-facing wall high in Death Canyon in Grand Teton National Park, around 8,000 feet, with many of the park's best non-summit rock routes. Twelve of the 14 climbs are alpine-style multipitch lines, and a couple are listed as trad. The south aspect makes it a useful early-season choice. Grades are mostly 5.10, with a few easier at 5.9 and several in the 5.11 range, and one reaching 5.12 or harder. Expect a long day: roughly three miles of canyon trail past Phelps Lake, then a scramble to a ledge, with alpine weather and route-finding in play. Rappels can snag in flakes.

_conflicts.wy_southwest_shoulder: Stored aspect is W; the page at https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/southwest-shoulder-climbing-at-devils-tower-wyoming says south facing.
_conflicts.wy_upper_devil_s_playground: Stored rock is granite; https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/upper-devils-playground-climbing-guide-vedauwoo-wyoming says conglomerate (Vedauwoo page describes granite-like rock).
_conflicts.wy_central_gorge: Stored rock is gneiss; https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106087336/central-gorge and https://mountainproject.com/area/106086552/shell-canyon say granite.
